results.title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta Madhya-līlā 1.76
results.translation: [This is a verse spoken by Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī.] “My dear friend, now I have met My very old and dear friend Kṛṣṇa on this field of Kurukṣetra. I am the same Rādhārāṇī, and now We are meeting together. It is very pleasant, but still I would like to go to the bank of the Yamunā beneath the trees of the forest there. I wish to hear the vibration of His sweet flute playing the fifth note within that forest of Vṛndāvana.”
results.purportStart: This verse also appears in the Padyāvalī (387), an anthology of verses compiled by Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī. results.title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta Madhya-līlā 1.79
results.translation: She thought of Him in the calm and quiet atmosphere of Vṛndāvana, dressed as a cowherd boy. But at Kurukṣetra He was in a royal dress and was accompanied by elephants, horses and crowds of men. Thus the atmosphere was not congenial for Their meeting.

results.title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta Madhya-līlā 1.86
results.translation: Absorbed in the ecstasy of the gopīs, Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu wished to see Lord Jagannātha in His original form as Kṛṣṇa, the son of Nanda Mahārāja, standing in Vṛndāvana and appearing very beautiful, His body curved in three places. His desire to see that form was always increasing.

results.title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta Madhya-līlā 1.87
results.translation: Just as Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī talked inconsistently with a bumblebee in the presence of Uddhava, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu in His ecstasy talked crazily and inconsistently day and night.
results.purportStart: This unmāda (madness) is not ordinary madness. When Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu talked inconsistently, almost like a crazy fellow, He was in the transcendental ecstasy of love. In the highest transcendental ecstasy there is a feeling of being enchanted in the presence of the enchanter. When the enchanter and the enchanted become separated, mohana, or bewilderment, occurs. When so bewildered due to sep

results.title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta Madhya-līlā 2.3
results.translation: During His last twelve years, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu always manifested all the symptoms of ecstasy in separation from Kṛṣṇa.

results.title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta Madhya-līlā 2.4
results.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu’s state of mind, day and night, was practically identical to Rādhārāṇī’s state of mind when Uddhava came to Vṛndāvana to see the gopīs.

results.title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta Madhya-līlā 2.5
results.translation: The Lord constantly exhibited a state of mind reflecting the madness of separation. All His activities were based on forgetfulness, and His talks were always based on madness.

results.title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta Madhya-līlā 2.7
results.translation: The small room beyond the corridor is called the Gambhīrā. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu used to stay in that room, but He did not sleep for a moment. All night He used to grind His mouth and head on the wall, and His face sustained injuries all over.

results.title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta Madhya-līlā 2.8
results.translation: Although the three doors of the house were always closed, the Lord would nonetheless go out and sometimes would be found at the Jagannātha temple, before the gate known as Siṁha-dvāra. And sometimes the Lord would fall flat into the sea.

results.title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta Madhya-līlā 2.9
results.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu would also run very fast across the sand dunes, mistaking them for Govardhana. As He ran, He would wail and cry loudly.
results.purportStart: Because of the winds of the sea, sometimes the sand would form dunes. Such sand dunes are called caṭaka parvata. Instead of seeing these sand dunes simply as hills of sand, the Lord would take them to be Govardhana Hill. Sometimes He would run toward these dunes at high speed, crying very loudly, expressing the state of mind exhibited by Rādhārāṇī. Thus Caitanya Mahāprabhu was absorbed in thoughts

results.title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta Madhya-līlā 2.11
results.translation: The extraordinary transformations of the body due to transcendental feelings would never have been possible for anyone but the Lord, in whose body all transformations were manifest.
results.purportStart: The ecstatic transformations of the body described in such exalted literatures as the Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu are practically not seen in this material world. However, these symptoms were perfectly present in the body of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. These symptoms are indicative of mahābhāva, or the highest ecstasy. Sometimes sahajiyās artificially imitate these symptoms, but experienced devotees rejec

results.title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta Madhya-līlā 2.15
results.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu used to express His mind in this way: “Where is the Lord of My life, who is playing His flute? What shall I do now? Where should I go to find the son of Mahārāja Nanda?

results.title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta Madhya-līlā 2.16
results.translation: “To whom should I speak? Who can understand My disappointment? Without the son of Nanda Mahārāja, My heart is broken.”

results.title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta Madhya-līlā 2.45
results.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu continued, “ ‘My dear friends, I have not the slightest tinge of love of Godhead within My heart. When you see Me crying in separation, I am just falsely exhibiting a demonstration of My great fortune. Indeed, not seeing the beautiful face of Kṛṣṇa playing His flute, I continue to live My life like an insect, without purpose.’

results.title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta Madhya-līlā 2.46
results.translation: “Actually, My love for Kṛṣṇa is far, far away. Whatever I do is actually an exhibition of pseudo love of Godhead. When you see Me cry, I am simply falsely demonstrating My great fortune. Please try to understand this beyond a doubt.

results.title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta Madhya-līlā 2.47
results.translation: “Even though I do not see the moonlike face of Kṛṣṇa as He plays on His flute, and although there is no possibility of My meeting Him, still I take care of My own body. That is the way of lust. In this way, I maintain My flylike life.
results.purportStart: In this connection, Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura says that the lovable Supreme Lord is the supreme shelter. The Lord is the supreme subject, and the devotees are the object. The coming together of a subject and object is called ālambana. The object hears, and the subject plays the flute. That the object cannot see the moonlike face of Kṛṣṇa and has no eagerness to see Him is the sign of

results.title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta Madhya-līlā 2.59
results.translation: “All these inauspicious days and nights are not passing, for I have not met You. It is difficult to know how to pass all this time. But You are the friend of the helpless and an ocean of mercy. Kindly give Me Your audience, for I am in a precarious position.”

results.title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta Madhya-līlā 2.63
results.translation: Because of the various kinds of ecstasy, contradictory states of mind occurred, and this resulted in a great fight between different types of ecstasy. Anxiety, impotence, humility, anger and impatience were all like soldiers fighting, and the madness of love of Godhead was the cause.
results.purportStart: In the Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu it is stated that when similar ecstasies from separate causes meet, they are called svarūpa-sandhi. When opposing elements meet, whether they arise from a common cause or different causes, their conjunction is called bhinna-rūpasandhi, the meeting of contradictory ecstasies. The simultaneous joining of different ecstasies — fear and happiness, regret and happiness — i

results.title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta Antya-līlā 14.1
results.translation: I shall now describe a very small portion of the activities performed by Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu with His mind, intelligence and body when He was bewildered by strong feelings of separation from Kṛṣṇa.

results.title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta Antya-līlā 14.15
results.translation: Such is the state of transcendental madness. Why is it difficult to understand? When one is highly elevated in love of Kṛṣṇa, he becomes transcendentally mad and talks like a madman.

results.title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta Antya-līlā 14.16
results.translation: “When the ecstatic emotion of enchantment gradually progresses, it becomes similar to bewilderment. Then one reaches the stage of astonishment [vaicitrī], which awakens transcendental madness. Udghūrṇā and citra-jalpa are two among the many divisions of transcendental madness.”
results.purportStart: This is a quotation from the Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi ( Sthāyibhāva-prakaraṇa 174). results.title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta Antya-līlā 14.60
results.translation: After some time, Svarūpa Dāmodara could no longer hear Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu chanting. When he entered the room, he found the three doors locked, but Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was gone.

results.title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta Antya-līlā 14.62
results.translation: After searching for some time, they came upon Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu lying in a corner by the northern side of the Siṁha-dvāra gate.

results.title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta Antya-līlā 14.64
results.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was lying unconscious, and His body had become elongated to five or six cubits. There was no breath from His nostrils.

results.title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta Antya-līlā 14.85
results.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu mistook the sand dune for Govardhana Hill and ran toward it.

results.title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta Antya-līlā 14.91
results.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was running with the speed of the wind, but He suddenly became stunned in ecstasy and lost all strength to proceed further.

results.title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta Antya-līlā 17.11
results.translation: All three doors were fastened as usual, but Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, in great ecstasy, nevertheless got out of the room and left the house.

results.title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta Antya-līlā 17.15
results.translation: After searching here and there, they finally came to the cow shed near the Siṁha-dvāra. There they saw Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu lying unconscious among the cows.

results.title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta Antya-līlā 17.16
results.translation: His arms and legs had entered the trunk of His body, exactly like those of a tortoise. His mouth was foaming, there were eruptions on His body, and tears flowed from His eyes.

results.title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta Antya-līlā 17.17
results.translation: As the Lord lay there unconscious, His body resembled a large pumpkin. Externally He was completely inert, but within He felt overwhelming transcendental bliss.

results.title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta Antya-līlā 17.20
results.translation: All the devotees began to chant the Hare Kṛṣṇa mantra very loudly in the Lord’s ears, and after a considerable time Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu regained consciousness.

results.title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta Antya-līlā 18.1
results.translation: In the brilliant autumn moonlight, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu mistook the sea for the river Yamunā. Greatly afflicted by separation from Kṛṣṇa, He ran and dove into the sea and remained unconscious in the water the entire night. In the morning, He was found by His personal devotees. May that Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, the son of mother Śacī, protect us by His transcendental pastimes.

results.title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta Antya-līlā 18.3
results.translation: While thus living at Jagannātha Purī, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu floated all day and night in an ocean of separation from Kṛṣṇa.

results.title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta Antya-līlā 18.27
results.translation: Brightened by the shining light of the moon, the high waves of the sea glittered like the waters of the river Yamunā.

results.title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta Antya-līlā 18.28
results.translation: Mistaking the sea for the Yamunā, the Lord ran swiftly and jumped into the water, unseen by the others.

results.title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta Antya-līlā 18.32
results.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu fully merged in the pastimes Lord Kṛṣṇa performed with the gopīs in the waters of the Yamunā.

results.title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta Antya-līlā 18.39
results.translation: In separation from the Lord, everyone felt as though he had lost his very life. The devotees concluded that there must have been some mishap. They could not think of anything else.

results.title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta Antya-līlā 19.60
results.translation: In ecstasy, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu rubbed His face against the walls all night long, making a peculiar sound, “goṅ-goṅ,” which Svarūpa Dāmodara could hear through the door.

results.title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta Antya-līlā 19.63
results.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu replied, “I was in such anxiety that I could not stay in the room. I wanted to go out, and therefore I wandered about the room, looking for the door.

results.title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta Antya-līlā 19.64
results.translation: “Unable to find the door, I kept hitting the four walls with My face. My face was injured, and it bled, but I still could not get out.”

results.title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta Antya-līlā 20.3
results.translation: While Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu thus resided at Jagannātha Purī [Nīlācala], He was continuously overwhelmed, night and day, by separation from Kṛṣṇa.

results.title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta Antya-līlā 20.39
results.translation: “ ‘My Lord Govinda, because of separation from You, I consider even a moment a great millennium. Tears flow from My eyes like torrents of rain, and I see the entire world as void.’

results.title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta Antya-līlā 20.41
results.translation: “The three worlds have become void because of separation from Govinda. I feel as if I were burning alive in a slow fire.

results.title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta Antya-līlā 20.47
results.translation: “ ‘Let Kṛṣṇa tightly embrace this maidservant who has fallen at His lotus feet, or let Him trample Me or break My heart by never being visible to Me. He is a debauchee, after all, and can do whatever He likes, but still He alone, and no one else, is the worshipable Lord of My heart.’

results.title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta Antya-līlā 20.52
results.translation: “I do not mind My personal distress. I only wish for the happiness of Kṛṣṇa, for His happiness is the goal of My life. However, if He feels great happiness in giving Me distress, that distress is the best of My happiness.
results.purportStart: Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura says that a devotee does not care about his own happiness and distress; he is simply interested in seeing that Kṛṣṇa is happy, and for that purpose he engages in various activities. A pure devotee has no way of sensing happiness except by seeing that Kṛṣṇa is happy in every respect. If Kṛṣṇa becomes happy by giving him distress, such a devotee accepts that u

results.title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta Antya-līlā 20.60
results.translation: “Service to My lover is the home of happiness and is more sweet than direct union with Him. The goddess of fortune is evidence of this, for although she constantly lives on the heart of Nārāyaṇa, she wants to render service to His lotus feet. She therefore considers herself a maidservant and serves Him constantly.”

results.title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta Antya-līlā 20.62
results.translation: The pure devotional service in Vṛndāvana is like the golden particles in the river Jāmbū. In Vṛndāvana there is not a trace of personal sense gratification. It is to advertise such pure love in this material world that Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu has written the previous verse and explained its meaning.
results.purportStart: The verse-referred to here is text 47, the eighth verse of the Śikṣāṣṭaka. results.title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta Antya-līlā 20.64
results.translation: The Lord had formerly composed these eight verses to teach people in general. Now He personally tasted the meaning of the verses, which are called the Śikṣāṣṭaka.

results.title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta Antya-līlā 20.65
results.translation: If anyone recites or hears these eight verses of instruction by Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, his ecstatic love and devotion for Kṛṣṇa increase day by day.

results.title: Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta Antya-līlā 20.69
results.translation: For twelve years, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu remained in that state day and night. With His two friends He tasted the meaning of those verses, which consists of nothing but the transcendental bliss and mellows of Kṛṣṇa consciousness. Texts 67-68
